landmarks.name: Botschaft der Vereinigten Staaten
landmarks.text: Pariser Platz 2, on the plot the embassy held from 1939. It stood empty inside the death strip for twenty eight years and the new house opened on 4 July 2008.

landmarks.name: Brandenburg Gate
landmarks.text: Carl Gotthard Langhans finished this sandstone gate in 1791 as a city toll gate, and for twenty eight years after 1961 it stood walled off inside the death strip.

landmarks.name: Reichstag
landmarks.text: Burned in 1933, shelled to a shell in 1945 and given a walkable glass dome by Norman Foster in 1999, so that the public literally stands above the parliament.

landmarks.name: Holocaust Memorial
landmarks.text: Peter Eisenman set 2711 concrete stelae on undulating ground in 2005. There is no prescribed path and no inscription, only the field.

landmarks.name: Unter den Linden
landmarks.text: The lime tree avenue laid out in 1647 so the Elector could ride from his palace to the Tiergarten hunting ground without leaving the shade.

landmarks.name: Bebelplatz
landmarks.text: On 10 May 1933 students burned some twenty thousand books here. Micha Ullman sunk an empty white library under the square as the memorial.

landmarks.name: Gendarmenmarkt
landmarks.text: Two matching cathedrals, French and German, flank Schinkel concert hall on what is widely called the most beautiful square in Berlin.

landmarks.name: Berlin Cathedral
landmarks.text: The Hohenzollern court church of 1905, its copper dome burnt out in 1944 and not fully restored until 1993.

landmarks.name: Museum Island
landmarks.text: Five museums built between 1830 and 1930 on a sandbank in the Spree, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1999.

landmarks.name: Fernsehturm
landmarks.text: At 368 metres the tallest structure in Germany, opened in 1969. Berliners named the cross that sunlight throws on its sphere the Pope revenge.

landmarks.name: Potsdamer Platz
landmarks.text: Europe busiest intersection in the 1920s, a minefield after 1961, and a brand new quarter of towers after 1993.

landmarks.name: The Spree
landmarks.text: The river the city was founded on, running 400 kilometres from Lusatia to the Havel and moving so slowly it sometimes flows backwards.
